trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one pops on its own. There is no separate task: the platinum is the reward for finishing everything else in this guide. Work the roadmap in order — story first, then collectibles, activities, and money — and save the 100% completion gold for last, since it is the longest grind.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first mission of the game, so this trophy comes naturally in the opening minutes. No special steps: play through the mission until it ends.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Chapter trophies pop when the chapter's final mission ends, so just follow the story. If you are chasing the missables, do the story-moment ones (Retail Therapy, Hot Together, Capital Offense) while the relevant characters are still around.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Same as the other chapter trophies: it pops when the chapter closes. Keep an eye on the missables list during this stretch — the partner-based trophies need a partner beside you, and partners come and go with the story.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. The chapter trophies cannot be missed: finishing the chapter is the requirement, and the story always takes you there.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale. Once it pops, the endgame cleanup begins: collectibles, activities, and the money trophies are best done in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission of the story. It is a gold trophy, but the task is the same as the chapter trophies: play the story to its end. After it pops, free roam opens up fully for the cleanup stages.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies pop when the mission ends, with no extra objective to hit. If a mission can be replayed from the mission list, a failed run costs nothing but time — this one cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish the mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are story beats: follow the objectives until the mission ends and the trophy pops. No side objective is needed for the trophy itself.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Child's Play. Like every mission trophy, it is awarded for completing the mission, not for how you complete it.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Headliners. Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the mission VCIA Takedown. The airport setting matters for one other trophy too: Catch Me If You Can, the unscheduled departure from VCIA, is flagged missable in this guide — watch for your chance around the airport while you are here.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Operation Savage Glory. A mission-completion trophy: play it through to the end.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion. This is the long one: it counts story missions, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and challenges together. Treat it as the last gold before the platinum — finish the other four roadmap stages first, then check the in-game completion stat to see what is left. The exact checklist behind the percentage is the game's own; this guide's stages cover everything the trophy descriptions name.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, long airtime, and the like. Stunts count across the whole game, so they pile up naturally while you drive between objectives; to grind them, chain jumps off ramps and highway crests in a fast car. PSN tracks the count to 250, so check the trophy's progress on PSN to see how far along you are.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types once. The activities are the game's side pastimes — races, fishing, arcade games, bowling, the shooting range, drone races, and the rest. One try each is enough: you do not need to win or finish them, just sample each type. If you are unsure which types you have tried, the activities you have already done for other trophies (fishing, bowling, arcade) count toward it.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Find the shooting ranges across Leonida and work through their challenges, aiming for gold on each. This is a skill trophy: learn each challenge's target pattern, use the range's own weapons, and retry — ranges can be revisited, so nothing here is missable. Do it after the story, when you have the full weapon set.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Drone races are one of the activity types: find each location, learn its gates, and win once per location. Losing a race costs nothing — retry as often as you like, and visit the locations in any order.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Races count per event, so you need 20 distinct race events, not 20 wins of the same one. Work through the race list across Leonida — street, off-road, and water races all count as races. A win in each is enough; you do not need to win them all in a row.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the activities: find a fishing spot, take the challenge against Cal, and out-fish him. If you lose, challenge him again — fishing challenges can be retried, so keep at it until you win.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game. Visit an arcade, pick any game, and play it to its end — winning is not required, completing is. This is also one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so it pulls double duty.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's last mission. Stranger missions unlock as you meet people across Leonida; follow Andy's strand to its final mission and complete it. The stranger strands are tracked under Strangers & Freaks — 8 strands in all — so Andy's is one of the eight.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's last mission. Same pattern as the other stranger finals: follow Kenton's strand to the end. If a stranger's missions stop appearing, explore more of the map — new strands open as you reach new areas.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's last mission. Billy's strand is one of the five named stranger finals in this guide; complete it and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Strangers appear all over the state — the five named finals (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus three more strands you find by exploring. Work through each strand to its final mission; the silver pops when the eighth strand closes. Strands can be done any time after they unlock, in any order.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's last mission. One of the five named stranger finals; follow Randy's strand to its end.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's last mission. The fifth named stranger final; complete it to close out Tyrone's strand.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are scattered over the map — scenic lookouts and quiet places. Visit each one and meditate; the count is tracked, so you can do it in any order and check your progress as you go. Pair this with The Goodtime State (explore all 52 areas) since both reward covering the map.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's hunt is a one-off target: find the animal's territory, track it, and take it down. The animal is unique, so the hunt is a single event — but it can be retried if you fail, and Bret's strand stays open until you finish it.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida — in shops, houses, and out-of-the-way places. Collect enough to finish three full sets; the silver pops on the third. Cards stay where they are until you pick them up, so nothing is missable — sweep the map area by area after the story.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK spots are spread across Leonida — the count is large, so treat it as a map sweep: work district by district and let the tally climb. The spots stay put until you use them, so take your time and pair it with the other map collectibles.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Finish 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's side objectives — the scattered tasks the game tracks alongside the main path. They accumulate across every activity, so play broadly: races, stunts, hunting, and the rest all feed the count. Check the challenges list in-game to see which ones you have left.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escape. You need a partner beside you when the heat hits four stars, then you both have to break the line of sight and get away clean. MISSABLE: partners are only available during parts of the story, so do this while a partner is with you in free roam — after the story, a partner may not be around. If the mission list lets you replay a partner mission, that is the fallback; it is not confirmed in-game.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. Pick three shops close together, hit them in a row with your partner, and keep the wanted level alive the whole time — losing it between shops breaks the chain. MISSABLE: it needs a partner, and partners are story-limited, so do it while one is available in free roam. Plan the route first, then run it in one go.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Every new vehicle you drive counts — cars, bikes, boats, and aircraft. The count climbs fastest by driving everything you see instead of sticking to one car: hop into new vehicles as you pass them. Nothing is missable; the map is full of vehicles to find.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Wait for a crowded fight — a gang shootout or a wanted-level standoff — trigger Combat Focus, and drop five enemies before it ends. If you fall short, retry: Combat Focus recharges, and fights are everywhere, so this is a matter of picking the right moment.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport. The description points at a specific moment: leaving the airport in a way the schedule does not plan — most likely by taking a plane during or around the VCIA Takedown mission. MISSABLE: if the moment is tied to that mission, do it while the mission is live; after it, the chance may be gone. If the mission list lets you replay VCIA Takedown, replay it for this trophy — not confirmed in-game.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke, not an instruction: the trophy is about the Rhino tanks, most likely during a story sequence where they show up. MISSABLE: if the tanks only appear in one mission, that mission is your window — watch for it during the story and do whatever the moment asks. If tanks also appear at high wanted levels in free roam, that is the fallback; it is not confirmed in-game.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Go in quiet: no alarms, no witnesses raising the alarm, no cameras catching you. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, let the heat die down, and try again. Jewelry stores can be robbed in free roam, so this is retryable, not missable.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Bank vaults are the big robberies: crack the vault, grab the take, and get out clean five times. Each vault is its own job — plan the escape route before you go in, and do not linger once the alarm is up. All five can be done in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run routes across Leonida — intercept one, stop it, crack it open, and get away before the response arrives. Trucks respawn on their routes, so a failed attempt just means waiting for the next one.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. Every named area counts once you have been there — drive, fly, and sail the whole map until the tally hits 52. This pairs with the other map trophies (100 vehicles, 100 WAiNK spots, 18 meditation spots): one long sweep of the state covers several of them at once.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Gangs run their own rackets across Leonida — find one operation per gang and hit it. The gangs are spread over the map, so this is another reason to cover the whole state. Operations can be retried, so work through the list at your own pace.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Find a bar on Ocean Beach with a view, order a cocktail, and take it in. It is a flavor trophy — a small moment, not a challenge. Any bar with the right view counts; if one does not trigger it, try another spot along the beach.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The description reads like a story beat — a getaway that starts inside a showroom and ends through its glass. MISSABLE: if the moment belongs to one mission, that mission is the only window — do it when the scene plays out and do not drive out gently. If showrooms can be smashed in free roam, that is the fallback; it is not confirmed in-game.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go bowling at the named alley — a full game, follow-through included. Bowling is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, and a visit here also feeds the activities count. If the first visit does not trigger it, finish a full game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague — it points at a story moment where the partnership lands in front of a crowd. Play the story and let it come: this is the kind of trophy that pops on its own during a set-piece. If it has not popped by the end of the story, check the missables page — it is listed there as a story moment to watch for.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — for better or worse. PSN tracks a count to 500, so this is a long grind, not a single decision: every choice you make across the game adds up. Play normally and the count climbs; dialogue options, side decisions, and approach choices all feed it. Because it is cumulative, it cannot be missed — it just takes time.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The name says it: fail at something once, then get it right the second time. MISSABLE: the trigger is likely a specific one-shot moment — if you succeed on the first try, there may be no second try to have. If it is tied to a story beat, it is flagged missable here; if it is a general mechanic (fail any attempt once, then succeed), it will come naturally. Our reading is a judgment from the description, not a confirmed fact — see the Sources page.
trophies.src: Official description (Exophase). Our advice from the official description — not yet checked in-game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the game's easter-egg trophy: something out of the ordinary, somewhere in Leonida. The description gives no location on purpose. Explore odd corners of the map — the places that look like they hide something — and the moment will find you. It is not missable: the strange thing stays strange until you see it.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by. Drive past a pedestrian and strike them with a melee weapon from the moving vehicle. It is a single clean hit — pick a slow, straight stretch with pedestrians nearby, line it up, and swing. If you miss, try again: pedestrians are everywhere.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies — bank vaults, armored trucks, shops — and your contacts turn them into clean money. Keep robbing, keep laundering, and the total climbs to $250,000. It pairs with the robbery trophies, so the money comes while you work the rest of the list.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Buy clothes, weapons, food, and gear — every shop purchase counts toward the total. The fastest route is the expensive end: high-end clothes and weapon upgrades burn through the total quickly. Money comes from the story and the robberies, so do this after you have built up cash.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are for sale across Leonida — buy every one. They cost money, so this pairs with the money trophies: earn first, then buy. Each garage also stores vehicles, which feeds the 100-vehicles discovery count.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles, open the Scooter Bros app, and register them — ten registrations in all. Any ten vehicles count, so register the ones you discover while working the 100-vehicles trophy; the two lists overlap nicely.
